title: Help
subtitle: Quick FAQ — how to use Atlas and the map

items.a: An interactive knowledge map about Claude — nodes (concepts), categories (colors), connections between them. Not an article: every node is an atomic unit of "what / why / when / how / example / mistakes".

A block with a short topic — one concept: an idea, feature, or pattern. Every node has details: what it is, why it matters, when to use it, how it affects results, an example request, and common mistakes.
5 colors = 5 topics: Basics, Configuration, Automation, Prompts, Agent scenarios. Lets you instantly see which type a node belongs to. The "Category: All" chip on top center filters by category.

items.q: How to read the connections between nodes?
items.a: Lines = related. Thin = hierarchy (parent → child). Dashed / accent = cross-links between branches that are worth reading together. The right-side panel shows a "Related" block per node.

items.q: What are Beginner / Intermediate / Expert levels?
items.a: Visibility slices by difficulty. Beginner shows only basic branches (5), Intermediate adds 4 more, Expert shows the full map (12). Change it in Profile → Level.

items.q: How to expand or collapse a node?
items.a: Click a node — toggles its children. Click again — back. Buttons at the bottom of the canvas: "Expand all" / "Collapse all" for bulk operations.
Quick command palette: ⌘+K (mac) or Ctrl+K (Windows). One search across nodes, tutorials, and prompts. ↑↓ to move, Enter to open, Esc to close.
The magnifier icon in the top-left header — click expands an input. Typing highlights matching nodes and auto-expands their ancestors. Esc clears the search.
The "Category: All" chip on top center. Click — dropdown with 5 categories. Nodes outside the chosen category become dim. "All" — removes the filter.
Drag the canvas with mouse/trackpad to pan. Mouse wheel or trackpad pinch — zoom. Buttons at the bottom: "−" / "+" / "Fit" (fit-to-screen) / "Reset" (100%, centered).

items.q: Tutorial vs. path — what's the difference?
items.a: A tutorial = step-by-step practice on one topic (5–10 steps, 10–30 min). A path = a sequence of 4–8 tutorials and nodes that leads to a specific goal (e.g., "From zero to Claude Code").
The "From zero to Claude Code" path — 6 steps, ~90 min. Covers: what Claude is → terminal → folders → installing Claude Code → first /init → first real prompt.

items.q: Where can I see my progress?
items.a: Profile (top-right) → "Claude tutorials" section. Progress bar + "N in progress" counter. Progress is stored locally in the browser (localStorage).

items.q: What to do after finishing a path?
items.a: Every tutorial ends with a "What's next" block with recommendations: next tutorials, related templates, deeper nodes. In Learning → Paths tab — all available routes.
Click a node → the DetailPanel opens on the right → bookmark icon in the panel header. One click — add, click again — remove. The icon switches to "filled" when bookmarked.

items.q: What are the "Viewed" and "Return later" marks?
items.a: In the DetailPanel under the title there are two buttons: "Viewed" = I got it; "Return later" = need to reread. Your personal flags so you don't get lost on repeat passes.

items.q: Where can I see my collections?
items.a: Profile → "Map" section: three counters — Viewed / Return later / Bookmarks. Clicking any number highlights the matching nodes directly on the map and expands their ancestors.

items.q: How to clear the highlight from the map?
items.a: Press Esc. That clears the temporary highlight triggered by clicking a profile stat. The map returns to normal mode.
Profile (top-right → user icon) → "Language" section. Available: RU / EN / FI. The locale is saved in the URL and localStorage — survives reload.
Profile → "Level" section: Beginner / Intermediate / Expert. Controls which map branches are visible by default. Below Expert some of the map is hidden.
Consecutive days you visit Atlas. Visit today after yesterday = streak +1. Miss a day — it resets. Profile shows current streak and total days.
Profile → "Data" section → "Export progress" downloads a JSON with all your bookmarks, marks, and tutorial progress. "Import" restores it on another device.
42 ready prompts across 9 categories and 3 difficulty levels. Open → fill in your context in [placeholders] → send to Claude. These are basic thinking forms — copy, adapt, reuse.

items.q: How to adapt a template to your task?
items.a: Don't copy as-is. Replace the [bracketed] placeholders with your data: product, audience, context. Otherwise Claude answers generically. The "Prompt techniques" tutorial digs deeper.

items.q: What do the template categories mean?
items.a: Analytics, content, development, learning, research, etc. — standard work tasks. Filter by category at the top of the Library to quickly find what you need instead of scrolling all 42.

items.q: What do the template levels mean?
items.a: Beginner — simple forms (role + task + format). Intermediate — with examples and constraints. Expert — advanced techniques: XML tags, Chain of Thought, Few-shot. Level filter is at the top-left of the Library.
